segments.text: > Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Smaller or lower-priority Node built-in modules, grouped here rather than given a full page each. Split out to its own page (rather than [PROCESS-CLI.md](PROCESS-CLI.md)) once it's substantial enough to need one.

notes: Surface: `.parse`, `.stringify`, `.escape`, `.unescape`, `.unescapeBuffer`, `.encode`, `.decode` — Node's `lib/querystring.js` in TypeScript ([ADR-01173](../adr/ADR-01173.md))
`.parse` returns a null-prototype object (a repeated key's values in an array), honours `sep`/`eq`/`maxKeys`/`decodeURIComponent`, and doesn't strip a leading `?` (unlike `new URLSearchParams(str)`)
`.stringify` takes an object (an array value repeats its key), with `sep`/`eq`/`encodeURIComponent`

caveats: `equal`/`strictEqual` and `deepEqual`/`deepStrictEqual` (and their `not*` counterparts) are aliases of each other — this compiler's `==` has no implicit coercion to distinguish them
`deepStrictEqual`: Map/Set/class instances, nullable-scalar members, and TypedArrays are a clean compile error (V1)
`.match`/`.doesNotMatch`'s regexp argument must be statically a RegExp ([ADR-00428](../adr/ADR-00428.md))
`.throws` only checks that *something* was thrown, not the thrown value's type/message
No `assert.rejects`/`doesNotReject` (needs await-a-rejection machinery) and no `AssertionError` class ([ADR-00499](../adr/ADR-00499.md))
notes: Surface: `.ok`, bare `assert(cond, msg?)`, `.equal`/`.strictEqual`, `.notEqual`/`.notStrictEqual`, `.deepEqual`/`.deepStrictEqual` (+`not*`), `.fail`, `.throws`, `.doesNotThrow`, `.ifError`, `.match`/`.doesNotMatch`
`deepStrictEqual` covers scalars, strings, arrays, and objects (recursively, incl. nested)

caveats: **Run-at-registration**: top-level code after a `test()` runs after it here, before it in Node. See [TDD-00140](../tdd/TDD-00140.md), [ADR-00419](../adr/ADR-00419.md)
`beforeEach`/`afterEach` are single slots (last wins) and also fire for subtests
No `mock.*`, `t.plan`, `run()`, concurrency, or snapshots
`mustCall` rejects rest-parameter callbacks (a rest tail is not a fixed ABI slot list) ([ADR-00496](../adr/ADR-00496.md))
`mustNotCall()` returns a `() => void`; using it where a non-zero-arity callback is expected is a type mismatch
`mustSucceed` is count-only (the "err is falsy" check is deferred); `expectWarning` runs the thunk but doesn't capture warnings
notes: Surface: the **runner**: `test`/`it`, `describe`/`suite`, TestContext `t.test`/`t.after`/`t.skip`/`t.todo`/`t.diagnostic`, hooks `before`/`after`/`beforeEach`/`afterEach` — plus the native helpers `mustCall`/`mustCallAtLeast`/`mustNotCall`/`skip`/`expectsError` + env probes
`mustCall` wraps every fixed callback signature — arrays, nullable scalars, any arity ([ADR-00496](../adr/ADR-00496.md))

`import { mustCall } from 'test'` — a first-class builtin (not Node's internal `../common`). `mustCall(fn, n=1)` — plus Node's function-less `mustCall()`/`mustCall(n)` forms, which count a synthesized noop ([ADR-00423](../adr/ADR-00423.md)) — wraps `fn` so its invocation count is verified at process exit (via the existing exit sink); an unmet/exceeded count prints a diagnostic and exits non-zero, giving examples/tests real async assertions instead of `console.log`. See [TDD-00122](../tdd/TDD-00122.md)/[ADR-00370](../adr/ADR-00370.md)

Distinct from `console.assert` (see [CONSOLE.md](CONSOLE.md)) — throws a catchable `AssertionError` (kind-tagged as a base `Error`, since this compiler's fixed error-kind enum has no dedicated slot) instead of logging and continuing

caveats: `.promisify` wraps a function value (a program's own, or a module written in TypeScript's); a code-generated builtin (`zlib.gzip`, `child_process.exec`, `fs.readFile`) is not a function value to pass it; `promisify.custom` is not read
`.format` requires a string-**literal** format (compile-time walk); a runtime format string is a compile error
`.inspect`'s options object is accepted but ignored (no `depth`/`colors`)
notes: Surface: `.inspect`, `.format`, `.promisify` (Node's `lib/internal/util.js`, in TypeScript: the callback's first argument rejects, its second resolves; a non-function is `ERR_INVALID_ARG_TYPE`) ([ADR-01172](../adr/ADR-01172.md))
`.inspect` reuses the same value formatter as `console.log` (strings single-quoted, `ClassName { … }`, arrays, `10n`)
`.format`: `%s`/`%d`/`%i`/`%f`/`%j`/`%o`/`%O`/`%%`, excess args appended space-separated, unrecognized specifiers left literal — matching Node

caveats: BlockList, SocketAddress and happy-eyeballs address selection (`autoSelectFamily`) are not ported
Windows keeps the earlier code-generated `net` (the TCP handles are POSIX sockets)
notes: Node's `lib/net.js` ported to TypeScript (`lib/node/net.ts`) over native TCP handles on the event loop: Socket (a Duplex — back-pressure, `'drain'`, pause/resume, `setEncoding`, `setTimeout`, `ref`/`unref`), Server (`listen` by port/host/backlog/options or a Unix-socket path, dual-stack `::` by default, `'listening'`/`'error'` on the next tick, `maxConnections`, `getConnections`), `connect`/`createConnection` (port, options, `{ path }`), `isIP`/`isIPv4`/`isIPv6`; errors built as Node builds them ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))

caveats: `udp4` only — no `udp6`
No `'listening'`/`'error'` events, options object, or multicast
Message listeners must be arrow/function-expression literals
`socket.send(msg, port, host)` positional form only — no `(msg, offset, length, port, address, cb)` form; no `.setTTL()`/membership methods
notes: Surface: UDP sockets: `createSocket('udp4')`, `bind`, `address()`, `setBroadcast()`, `on('message')`, `send`, `close`
Each socket's fd folds into the same `select()` event loop as `net`/`child_process` ([ADR-00327](../adr/ADR-00327.md))

`.address()` reports the real bound `{ address, family, port }` via `getsockname` (the `bind(0)` ephemeral-port idiom); `.setBroadcast(flag)` is a real `setsockopt(SO_BROADCAST)` — required before sending to a broadcast address ([ADR-00581](../adr/ADR-00581.md))
`'message'` fires with a Buffer and an rinfo `{ address, port }`; `send(msg, port, host)` resolves `host` (name or IP) via the `dns` helper
`msg`/`send` payloads take a string/Buffer/ArrayBuffer/DataView

caveats: OpenSSL-only (libssl) — a `-crypto=commoncrypto` build using `tls` is a clean compile error (Mac's CommonCrypto has no TLS API)
Session resumption, OCSP, renegotiation, PSK and `getPeerCertificate()`'s certificate object are not ported
Windows keeps the earlier code-generated, blocking `tls`
notes: Node's `_tls_wrap` shape in TypeScript (`lib/node/tls.ts`): a TLSSocket is a net.Socket whose handle carries a non-blocking OpenSSL session — `tls.connect` (`servername`, `rejectUnauthorized`, `ca`/`cert`/`key`, ALPN; `'secureConnect'`, `authorized`/`authorizationError`, Node's verify error codes and messages), `tls.createServer` (`'secureConnection'`, `'tlsClientError'`), `createSecureContext`, `getProtocol`/`getCipher` ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))

caveats: `dns.resolve4`/`resolve` use `getaddrinfo` (the OS resolver), not real DNS `A` queries — no `resolve6`/`resolveMx`/`resolveTxt`/`reverse`
IPv4 (`AF_INET`) only; `family` is always 4
The callback forms fire synchronously, not on a later event-loop tick
Failure passes a generic `Error` (`getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND`), not a `code`-tagged Node error
notes: Surface: `dns.lookup`, `dns.resolve4`/`resolve`, `dns.promises.lookup`

`getaddrinfo(3)`-backed ([ADR-00326](../adr/ADR-00326.md), [ADR-00329](../adr/ADR-00329.md)); `lookup` returns one dotted-quad, `resolve4` all A records as a `string[]`, `promises.lookup` a `Promise<{address, family}>`
Verified on Mac (arm64) with the Darwin `struct addrinfo` `ai_addr`/`ai_next` offsets probed on the machine — the same layout the WebSocket-client resolver still gates out on Darwin

caveats: The callback form fires synchronously, not deferred to the next event-loop tick
No Brotli (`brotliCompress*`) — it would pull in `-lbrotli`, a new system dependency this binding deliberately avoids
No class/stream forms (`createGzip()`, `zlib.Gzip`, …) — the WHATWG `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` cover the streaming case ([STREAMS.md](STREAMS.md))
`{ level }` is the only supported option and must be a compile-time constant
notes: Surface: `gzip`/`gunzip`, `deflate`/`inflate`, `deflateRaw`/`inflateRaw`, `unzip`, each `*Sync` + `(err, result)` callback
One-shot calls over the same libz backend as `CompressionStream` ([ADR-00302](../adr/ADR-00302.md)), driven by a shared `@__kml_zlib_oneshot` helper ([ADR-00321](../adr/ADR-00321.md))
Input may be a Buffer/TypedArray, ArrayBuffer, DataView, or string (UTF-8); output is always a Buffer
Surface: `vm.Script`, sandboxed `eval`-like execution
Same fundamental blocker as the already-tracked bare `eval()` — see [GLOBAL-FUNCTIONS.md](GLOBAL-FUNCTIONS.md). Opt-in embedded-engine path scoped in [TDD-00046](../tdd/TDD-00046.md), not started

caveats: Messages are **strings** (serialize with `JSON.stringify`) — a typed subset can't hand arbitrary object shapes to unknown subscribers
Subscriber params must be string-typed (an untyped pre-wrapped subscriber is a clean rejection, never silent reinterpretation)

`tracingChannel` and the store bindings (`bindStore`/`runStores`) are clean rejections; a Channel handle isn't module-global-promotable (capture it in a closure, not a named top-level function) ([ADR-00420](../adr/ADR-00420.md))
notes: Surface: `channel`/`subscribe`/`unsubscribe`/`hasSubscribers`, Channel `.publish`/`.hasSubscribers`/`.name`
Name-keyed pub/sub; 0/1/2-arity subscribers, pointer-identity unsubscribe

caveats: `http.request(new URL(…))` is not accepted — a `string | URL | options` parameter is a union code generation cannot tell apart ([BACKLOG](../BACKLOG.md))
notes: Node's `_http_agent`/`_http_client` in TypeScript (`lib/node/internal_http.ts`) over `net`: ClientRequest (an OutgoingMessage — chunked bodies, `'response'`/`'socket'`/`'information'`/`'upgrade'`/`'error'`, `abort`/`destroy`/`setTimeout`), Agent with keep-alive pooling (`http.globalAgent` keeps sockets alive and unref'd, as Node 19+), `IncomingMessage` responses as Readables ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))

caveats: Same client limit as `http` for a `URL` argument ([BACKLOG](../BACKLOG.md))
notes: `https.createServer` is a `tls.Server` running the http module's connection handling; `https.request`/`get`/`Agent`/`globalAgent` connect with `tls.connect` ([ADR-01170](../adr/ADR-01170.md))
Surface: re-exports: `ReadableStream`/`WritableStream`/`TransformStream`/`CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream`

The names bind as identity to the ambient WHATWG constructors that already exist — importing them is interchangeable with the globals ([ADR-00410](../adr/ADR-00410.md)); the queuing-strategy classes are not exported

caveats: `setupPrimary`'s `exec`/`execArgv` are a compile-time rejection — workers re-exec this compiled program itself, so there is no separate script file for a worker to run (a genuine impossibility of native compilation, [ADR-01015](../adr/ADR-01015.md)); `args` and `silent` work on every platform, Windows included ([ADR-01018](../adr/ADR-01018.md))

`'online'` fires from a queued microtask (the worker is exec'd by then), not a wire handshake; `cluster.workers` iterates and indexes by id but is not a real id-keyed *object* (no `Object.keys` over it)
On Darwin, `SO_REUSEPORT` accept distribution is uneven (often one worker) — correctness holds, balancing differs from Linux's kernel load-balancing
Can't be combined with Worker threads (same restriction as `http.listen({workers})`)
In a worker, `cluster.worker` exposes `.id`; its `.process` and messaging methods are not available on it (use the global `process`)
notes: Surface: `fork`, worker messaging (strings AND objects/arrays/numbers/booleans — Node's json serialization mode, both directions, [ADR-01015](../adr/ADR-01015.md)), `isPrimary`/`isWorker`/`worker`, `Worker.id`/`.process`, cluster-level `cluster.on('fork'/'online'/'message'/'exit'/'disconnect'/'listening')` (listeners get the Worker first, either registration order; 'listening' passes Node's `{ address, port, addressType }`), `cluster.workers` (live — a reaped worker is dropped BEFORE its `'exit'` listeners run, like Node — with `cluster.workers[id]` lookup), `cluster.disconnect(cb?)` (flushes in-flight messages), `setupPrimary({ args, silent })` + `cluster.settings` ([ADR-01012](../adr/ADR-01012.md)/[ADR-01015](../adr/ADR-01015.md))
Several listeners per event coexist in registration order — `worker.on(...)` lists plus the cluster-level relays ([ADR-01015](../adr/ADR-01015.md))
Workers each bind the port via `SO_REUSEPORT`
Unifies with `http.listen({ workers: N })`'s worker-id global — the primary stays in the event loop while workers live (their IPC handles), then blocks in `waitpid` as the backstop

Workers carry the TDD-00141 fork IPC channel ([ADR-00427](../adr/ADR-00427.md)): `worker.send`/`.on('message'/'online'/'exit'/'close'/'error')`/`.disconnect()`/`.kill()`/`.destroy()`/`.process.pid`; in-worker `process.send`/`process.on('message')`

caveats: `http2.createServer`/`createSecureServer` `(req, res)` handlers don't receive the request body — `req.on('data')`/`req.stream()` isn't wired to the h2 body (the `klain:http` `http.listen` h2 path delivers it as one buffered `req.body` chunk; TDD-00218)
`stream.close()`/`setEncoding`/`resume`/`pause` are accepted no-ops; responses are written when the handler returns (no mid-stream RST/flow control)
Client `http2.connect` is h2c only — a TLS authority throws
Client requests are body-less (END_STREAM at submit) — `req.write`/`end(body)` are clean rejections
Client response `':status'` arrives as a *string* in the headers map (Node types it as a number); session/stream `'error'`/`'close'` listeners are accepted no-ops
`getDefaultSettings`/`getPackedSettings`/`getUnpackedSettings`: the invalid-value `RangeError` taxonomy is not modeled
`createSecureServer` h2 connections are served one-at-a-time (the TLS drive is blocking in the accept path)
Server/client push streams are unsupported ([TDD-00139](../tdd/TDD-00139.md))
notes: Surface: `http2.createServer`/`createSecureServer`/`connect`, `Http2Session`/`Http2Stream`

Server-side Stages 1–2: `http2.createServer` on the http server handle serves **h2c** (also answers 1.1, a superset of Node); compat `.on('request', (req, res))` and the core streams API — `.on('stream', (stream, headers))` with pseudo-headers on the map, `stream.respond({ ':status', … })` incl. response headers, `.end`/`.write`. See [TDD-00139](../tdd/TDD-00139.md), [ADR-00414](../adr/ADR-00414.md), [ADR-00415](../adr/ADR-00415.md)
Client (Stage 3): `http2.connect("http://…")` → session `.request({ ':path', ':method', headers… })` → stream `.on('response'\|'data'\|'end')`

Stage 4: `http2.constants` compile-time namespace (header/method names, RFC 7540 error codes; unknown members reject cleanly); `getDefaultSettings`/`getPackedSettings`/`getUnpackedSettings` produce nghttp2 wire format

`createSecureServer({ cert, key }[, handler])` serves **h2 over TLS**: each accepted fd is TLS-handshaken, ALPN selects `h2`, driving the same nghttp2 session as h2c over `SSL_read`/`SSL_write` shims; compat and `.on('stream')` APIs inherited unchanged. A client that doesn't negotiate `h2` is dropped after the handshake (Node's `allowHTTP1:false` default) unless `allowHTTP1: true` serves it over the HTTPS/1.1 fiber path. See [TDD-00111](../tdd/TDD-00111.md) Stage 3b, [ADR-00504](../adr/ADR-00504.md), [ADR-00505](../adr/ADR-00505.md)

Transparent h2, no `http2` import needed: `fetch` negotiates h2 over TLS (ALPN); `http.listen` serves **h2c** (cleartext prior-knowledge) alongside 1.1, riding nghttp2 (`http2src/http2.c`, linked when `http.listen` is used), the h2 preface detected per-connection and dispatched through the shared 1.1 handler. h2-over-TLS is served explicitly via `http2.createSecureServer`; async handlers under h2 remain unsupported ([TDD-00111](../tdd/TDD-00111.md) Stage 3b, [ADR-00357](../adr/ADR-00357.md))
Surface: `AsyncLocalStorage`, `AsyncResource`

`AsyncLocalStorage<T>`: `run`/`getStore`/`exit`/`enterWith`/`disable` with real context propagation **across `await`** — the store lives in the coroutine task struct, so a value set with `run(...)` survives an await/park/resume and a spawned task inherits it ([ADR-00678](../adr/ADR-00678.md)); a `setTimeout`/`setInterval` scheduled inside `run(...)` carries it to its fire ([ADR-00679](../adr/ADR-00679.md))

Static `AsyncLocalStorage.bind(fn)` (a wrapper of `fn`'s own signature that reinstalls the captured context) and `AsyncResource` (`runInAsyncScope`, capturing at construction) capture-and-replay the context ([ADR-00680](../adr/ADR-00680.md))
`getStore()` on an unset/disabled store is a real `undefined` typed `T | undefined`, distinguishable from a genuine `0`/`""`/null store ([ADR-00782](../adr/ADR-00782.md))
caveats: `AsyncLocalStorage.snapshot()` is a clean rejection — its runner is fully generic (parameter/return types vary per call site), needing generic first-class closures this compiler doesn't have

`AsyncResource.runInAsyncScope(fn, thisArg, …)` accepts `thisArg` but does not bind it (closures carry no dynamic `this`); a `run(...)` callback that throws does not restore the frame (exception-safe restore is a follow-up)
`.then`/`.catch` reaction callbacks and EventEmitter listeners do not yet propagate context (only `await`, task-spawn, and timers do)

The low-level `createHook`/`executionAsyncId`/`triggerAsyncId`/async-id lifecycle is out of scope — a compiled AOT binary has no V8 promise-hooks or GC-tracked async-ids (a faithful impossibility), so those stay clean rejections
